papers.title: Asymptotic normality and optimality in nonsmooth stochastic approximation

claims.label: Theorem 2.7 (Smooth Invertibility and Active Manifolds)
claims.statement_original:
Consider the set-valued map
\[
F(x):=A(x)+\partial f(x),
\]
where $A:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d$ is $C^p$-smooth and $f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{\infty\}$ is subdifferentially continuous near a point $\bar x$. Suppose that $f$ admits a $C^{p+1}$ active manifold $\mathcal M$ at some point $\bar x$ for $-A(\bar x)\in\widehat\partial f(\bar x)$. Let $G(x)=0$ be any $C^{p+1}$-smooth local defining equations for $\mathcal M$ near $\bar x$ and let $\widehat f$ be any $C^{p+1}$-smooth function that agrees with $f$ on a neighborhood of $\bar x$ in $\mathcal M$. Define the map
\[
\mathcal H(x,y):=A(x)+\nabla\widehat f(x)+\nabla G(x)^\top y.
\]
Then there exists a unique multiplier vector $\bar y$ satisfying the condition $0=\mathcal H(\bar x,\bar y)$. Moreover, $F$ is $C^p$-invertible around $(0,\bar x)$ with inverse $\sigma(\cdot)$ if and only if the matrix
\[
\Sigma:=P_{T_{\mathcal M}(\bar x)}\nabla_x\mathcal H(\bar x,\bar y)P_{T_{\mathcal M}(\bar x)}
\]
is nonsingular on $T_{\mathcal M}(\bar x)$, and in this case equality $\nabla\sigma(0)=\Sigma^\dagger$ holds.

claims.label: Theorem 3.1 (Sample average approximation)
claims.statement_original:
Suppose that Assumptions A and B hold. In particular, there exist $\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2>0$ and a $C^1$-smooth map $\sigma:B_{\epsilon_1}(0)\to B_{\epsilon_2}(\bar x)$ satisfying
\[
\operatorname{gph}\sigma=(B_{\epsilon_1}(0)\times B_{\epsilon_2}(\bar x))\cap\operatorname{gph}F^{-1}.
\]
Suppose moreover that there exists a square integrable function $L(z)$ satisfying
\[
\|\nabla A(x_1,z)-\nabla A(x_2,z)\|\le L(z)\|x_1-x_2\|\qquad\forall x_1,x_2\in B_{\epsilon_2}(\bar x).\tag{3.3}
\]
Shrinking $\epsilon_2$, if necessary, let us ensure that $\epsilon_2\le\min\left\{\frac{\operatorname{lip}(\sigma)^{-1}}{2\mathbb E L},\sqrt{\frac{\epsilon_1}{2\mathbb E L}}\right\}$. Let $S=\{z_1,\ldots,z_k\}$ be i.i.d samples drawn from $\mathcal P$ and let $x_k$ be a measurable selection of the solutions (3.2) such that $\Pr[x_k\in B_{\epsilon_2}(\bar x)]\to1$ as $k$ tends to infinity. Then asymptotic normality holds:
\[
\sqrt k(x_k-\bar x)\xrightarrow D\mathsf N\left(0,\nabla\sigma(0)\cdot\operatorname{Cov}(A(\bar x,z))\cdot\nabla\sigma(0)^\top\right).
\]

claims.label: Theorem 3.2 (Asymptotic optimality)
claims.statement_original:
Suppose that Assumption A and B hold. Let $\mathcal L:\mathbb R^d\to[0,\infty)$ be any symmetric, quasiconvex, and lower semicontinuous function, and let $\widehat x_k:\mathcal Z^k\to\mathbb R^d$ be a sequence of estimators. Then the inequality
\[
\lim_{c\to\infty}\liminf_{k\to\infty}\sup_{\mathcal P'\in\mathcal B_{c/k}}\mathbb E_k^{\mathcal P'}\left[\mathcal L\left(\sqrt k(\widehat x_k-\bar x_{\mathcal P'})\right)\right]\ge\mathbb E[\mathcal L(Z)]
\]
holds, where $Z\sim\mathsf N\left(0,\nabla\sigma(0)\cdot\operatorname{Cov}(A(\bar x,z))\cdot\nabla\sigma(0)^\top\right)$.

claims.label: Theorem 5.1 (Asymptotic Normality)
claims.statement_original:
Suppose that Assumption C, D, E, I, and J hold. Suppose that $\gamma\in(\frac12,1)$ and that the sequence $x_k$ generated by the process (4.2) converges to $\bar x$ with probability one. Suppose that there exists a constant $\mu>0$ satisfying
\[
\langle\nabla_{\mathcal M}F_{\mathcal M}(\bar x)v,v\rangle\ge\mu\|v\|^2\qquad\text{for all}\qquad v\in T_{\mathcal M}(\bar x).\tag{5.1}
\]
Then $F$ is $C^p$-smoothly invertible around $(\bar x,0)$ with inverse $\sigma(\cdot)$ and the average iterate $\bar x_k=\frac1k\sum_{i=1}^k x_i$ satisfies
\[
\sqrt k(\bar x_k-\bar x)\xrightarrow D N\left(0,\nabla\sigma(0)\cdot\Sigma\cdot\nabla\sigma(0)^\top\right).
\]
Moreover, $\nabla\sigma(0)$ can be equivalently written as $\nabla\sigma(0)=(P_{T_{\mathcal M}(\bar x)}\nabla_{\mathcal M}F_{\mathcal M}(\bar x)P_{T_{\mathcal M}(\bar x)})^\dagger$.
